Unknown action @GET. Did you mean @get?
Datastar reads an action only as @get( with nothing before the parenthesis. With a space the @ reaches the browser, which cannot parse it.
Datastar expression: Unexpected end of input
Empty Datastar expression.
Datastar reads $my-count as one signal named my-count, and nothing here declares it: a key my-count is the signal $myCount. For a subtraction write $my - count, with spaces.
No markup or code in the project defines the signal 'neverDefinedInTheForge'.
Datastar rewrites $count in a regular expression into $['count'], which changes the pattern. Build the pattern with new RegExp('...'): Datastar leaves a quoted string as written.
@clipboard is a Datastar Pro action; it needs the Pro bundle.
@post has no option contentTyp, so Datastar ignores it. Did you mean contentType?

Written on the wire as data-signals:foo-bar, which Datastar reads back as the signal $fooBar: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.
Datastar's client holds no null: in data-signals a null removes the key, so "selected" is not declared, and an expression that reads it gets "". Declare it with the value it starts as, such as "".
A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "is-open" at runtime. Write isOpen.
Streamlord refuses "foo__bar" at runtime: it contains __, where Datastar starts reading modifiers.

Written on the wire as data-on:widget-loaded__case.camel, which Datastar reads back as the event widgetLoaded: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.
Streamlord refuses "my-event__x" at runtime: it contains __, where Datastar starts reading modifiers.

Written on the wire as data-class:is-open__case.camel, which Datastar reads back as the class isOpen: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.
Streamlord refuses "isOpen_" at runtime: it ends in _, which runs into the __ of the modifiers after it, so Datastar's client would read the key as is-open.

Written on the wire as data-style:background-color, which Datastar reads back as the property background-color: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself. A CSS property is written in kebab-case: data-style:background-color.

Streamlord refuses "viewBox" at runtime: it has a capital, which the browser lowercases in an attribute name; write it as HTML has it, view-box or viewbox, or, for an attribute that has capitals such as SVG's viewBox, the object form dataAttr("{viewBox: ...}").
Streamlord refuses "über" at runtime: it is not a name a $ reference reaches: Datastar reads ASCII letters, digits and _, in parts joined by dots.
Streamlord refuses "a:b" at runtime: it is not a name a $ reference reaches: Datastar reads ASCII letters, digits and _, in parts joined by dots.
Streamlord refuses "constructor" at runtime: it has the part constructor, which every object already has, so the client cannot hold a signal there.

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "is-open" at runtime. Write isOpen, or ['is-open'] for a key with a hyphen in it.

Unknown Datastar attribute data-onn. Did you mean data-on?
Unknown modifier __debunce on data-on, which Datastar ignores, so it listens for the event click. Did you mean __debounce?
Datastar reads $my-value as one signal named my-value, and nothing here declares it: a key my-value is the signal $myValue. For a subtraction write $my - value, with spaces.
The browser lowercases attribute names, so this reaches Datastar as the event myevent, not myEvent. Write data-on:my-event__case.camel: keys are kebab-case.
This is an aliased Datastar attribute, but the prefix is set to data-. Check streamlord.attributePrefix.
data-bind declares the signal $count, as written, which holds the $ itself, so $count does not reach it: that reads the signal count.
data-persist is a Datastar Pro attribute; it needs the Pro bundle.
